thread:
jamie: FYI escalation from Zenly — intermittent 504s on their dedicated cluster (eu-gpu-ssd-5) starting 2026-03-15 ~22:00 UTC. They provided a small set of request IDs: req-20260315-9a7f2, req-20260315-b2c11, req-20260316-01ff3. Customer says latency spikes then 504, not consistent, affects billing. Need repro bundle + node metrics.

mona: Can we get a quick repro curl from the customer first so we can replay locally? Also need the pod name(s) and exact time windows. Ask them to include X-Request-Id header if possible. If they can't, we'll tie by request ids.

jamie: Pasted their minimal curl sample (they redacted API key) — asked them to run this locally and attach the output.
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: req-20260315-9a7f2" \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-4o","input":"short test"}'
```

kevin: If they can reproduce, request the full tcp dump and the response headers. Meanwhile preparing node-side collection steps — here's the checklist I need from ops on that dedicated cluster: pod logs (kubectl logs --previous), pod env (kubectl describe pod), kubelet journal, syslog, dmesg, and GPU metrics snapshot (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv,noheader -l 1 --count=5). Also request /var/log/kern.log for any XID errors.

li: Copying checklist into a one-liner for the on-call collector:
```
# pod/prefix from tenant
kubectl -n tenant-zenly get pods -o wide | grep zenly
kubectl -n tenant-zenly logs <pod> --all-containers --since=30m > pod-<pod>-logs.txt
kubectl -n tenant-zenly describe pod <pod> > pod-<pod>-describe.txt
journalctl -u kubelet --since "2026-03-15 21:45:00" > kubelet-journal.txt
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > dmesg.txt
sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 500 > kern.log.snip
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 --count=10 > nvidia-smi-sample.csv
# collect docker/containerd runtime logs on node
sudo journalctl -u containerd --since "2026-03-15 21:45:00" > containerd-journal.txt
```

mona: Also request the pod-level request tracing header if present: X-Request-Id, X-Trace-Id. If the customer uses our SDK, ask for sdk.trace_id in the payload. Tell them to run their curl with verbose (-v) and capture response headers.

jamie: Customer replied they ran the curl once and got a 504, attached verbose output: response includes "Connection timed out after 30001ms" and no body, but we see X-Request-Id echoed as req-20260315-9a7f2. They couldn't provide tcpdump (company policy), but allowed a support-collected debug bundle.

kevin: Ok start the support bundle workflow. On the node where the pod last ran, run the debug-agent to assemble: pod logs, node syslogs, kernel ring buffer, nvidia-smi history, kube-proxy logs, and the kubelet trace. Use the support-helper script to push to s3 with that run id. Example: 
```
sudo /opt/support-helper/collect --tenant zenly --cluster eu-gpu-ssd-5 \n  --since "2026-03-15T21:50:00Z" --until "2026-03-15T22:10:00Z" \n  --request-ids req-20260315-9a7f2,req-20260315-b2c11 \n  --out s3://redwood-support/zenly/3127777777/
```

infra-bot: support-helper job queued -> job-id: sh-3127777777-01, collector: kevin, target-node: eu-gpu-node-19, ETA ~6m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kevin: Starting collection on eu-gpu-node-19 now. I'll run nvidia-smi loop and capture kernel logs simultaneously. If we see any XID probs I'll escalate to eng-runtime.

mona: Reminder: for repro we also want a minimal synthetic load test hitting the same model/version and sequence length. If the customer can run a quick scripted loop (5-10 requests at their peak qps) that'll help reproduce. Provide them this script: 
```
for i in $(seq 1 5); do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "X-Request-Id: repro-$i" -d '{"model":"redwood-4o","input":"repro test"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate || true; \
  sleep 0.5
done
```

jamie: Customer OK'd the debug bundle collection. infra-bot later: support-helper upload complete -> s3://redwood-support/zenly/3127777777/support-bundle.tar.gz sha256: d1e8f3... :link:

kevin: Downloaded and started quick triage. Observations in first pass: node eu-gpu-node-19 shows GPU memory pressure peaks around 60-80% before the 504s, but no immediate ECC or XID kernel oops in the captured kern.log. There are a few kubelet restarts around 22:03 UTC that correspond to the time window. Dumping kubelet journal now and capturing kube-proxy errors.

li: I grepped the application logs in the bundle for request ids — we see the three supplied ids and they map to pod zenly-api-7f9c on node eu-gpu-node-19. The pod shows a 502/504 upstream from the runtime at the same timestamps.

mona: Next steps: 1) patch the pod to increase request timeout to 45s temporarily and see if we get a different behavior, 2) run a small synthetic load against that exact pod IP to see if we can trigger the 504 locally, 3) if kubelet keeps flapping, escalate to eng-sre for node stability.

jamie: I'll coordinate the timeout patch with the customer and schedule a controlled repro window tomorrow 22:00-22:30 UTC. If we still see 504s with kubelet stable, we'll open an eng-runtime ticket with the bundle and mark as P2.

kevin: noted. tagging @eng-runtime on the follow-up once we have repro steps. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket created -> #SUP-8452, linked bundle s3://redwood-support/zenly/3127777777/support-bundle.tar.gz

jamie: Thanks team — tracking here, will update with the controlled repro results.
